Filing gate: ① (review follow-ups, one card per PR) · Source: fleet (Contract review record 7196757117 on PR #37600, section ③ and its out-of-diff notes; read from code, not run)

## What happens

PR #37600 (Fixes #36595) makes `os validate` refuse an `objects.{parent}._relatedLists.{list}` key when the served tab list no longer labels that list. The review found two places where the tooling and the served read still disagree with that rule:

- [ ] **`os i18n extract` / `os i18n check` still expect the refused key.** Both walk the owner's `relatedLists` without applying a pair package's arrangement. In a stack that holds the owner and its pair, the coverage gate counts the owner-labelled key as expected while `os validate` refuses it, so an author cannot satisfy both. Expected: the extractor and the coverage walk apply the arrangement the way the registry serves it, so the three commands agree.
- [ ] **The object read hands no pair catalog.** Since #36574 the lint accepts a key over a list whose label an arrangement sets, but the `/meta/object` read passes no `pairBundle` (`servedOverrideBaseOf` answers none for `object` in `packages/rest/src/meta-item-read-gate.ts`), so such a label translates only when it equals the owner's text. The #36528 objectql pin passes a pair bundle by hand, and its header says the REST read supplies one, which the code contradicts. Expected: either the object read hands the pair's catalog, or the rule refuses those keys too, decided in one place.

Category ①: an author-facing command disagrees with the served read, so a key passes one gate and fails another, or is accepted and translates nothing.
Priority: p2, the grade of #36595.
Business reason: translators of a customised package see an untranslated tab title, or a coverage gate they cannot satisfy.
Reader: seat 2 area s2-ux-T (repo:objectstack#2), after PR #37600 merges.
Dedupe: `i18n extract relatedLists arrangement`, `pairBundle meta object read` (open issues), 0 hits.
Related: #36595, PR #37600, #36528, #36574.
